0.content:
Odette, the troupe's Prima Ballerina and a Fatuus, is Vodyanitsa's closest friend. Vodyanitsa hides backstage every rehearsal hoping to startle her and has never managed it, though she can tell Odette's dancing is flawless just by listening. She pushes up the corners of Odette's mouth to practise smiling for the Tsaritsa ("What. Great. News."), makes her read fan letters, drags her to feed the theater's stray cats (who sharpen their claws when Odette approaches), and clings to her arm when sick. Odette brings her mints and refuses to blow bubbles with her.

In the afterlife theater (7.0), when the Traveler said Odette was Lelek, Vodyanitsa was stunned that she had missed it and wanted to hug her for carrying so many identities. She told Odette none of them believed she would kill innocent people, and, after first questioning it, went along when Odette chose to reveal herself to the group. Afterward, the Rokot withdrew the Lelek codename and suspended Odette; Vodyanitsa keeps working with her. Odette, in turn, notices when the voices of the departed Water Imps trouble her and quietly keeps an eye on her.

Palomeya reports that Vodyanitsa once gift-wrapped a ticket to her own show for Odette, who returned it and bought her own. Odette is the only person known to dare return her gift. Odette says she overhears Vodyanitsa's worries because she talks in her sleep.

1.content:
Alyosha, a hunter, is Vodyanitsa's Rokot partner. He once did odd jobs at the theater and brought his dog Tugarin backstage, where she fed him treats. Later, on a Rokot mission where all were in disguise, Tugarin recognised her scent, and the two learned each other's identities and kept the secret. In 7.0 they recruited the Traveler together. She wonders whether his puppies understand her songs; her lullabies put them to sleep before the first verse ends.

In 7.1 she gave Alyosha a makeover as a frail old man so he could trap the Seal of Life seller, declaring he had "passed the test" once he grumbled about young people's manners. At Rankova Zorya his dogs help guard the station, though one, Lyumina, ran off when Vodyanitsa tried to make friends.

2.content:
The Rokot ("Rumble") is a secret civilian organisation working for the common people. Members use codenames, rarely know each other's identities, avoid violence and leak evidence of corruption to trigger official investigations. Vodyanitsa uses her theater access to gather intelligence from patrons. In 7.0 she and Alyosha recruited the Traveler with an application form approved by the Rokot's president, then targeted Chugunov, owner of the Iskra Manufacturing Plant, for illegal energy use and harsh working conditions.

Chugunov dodged her questions, so she met Mitya for tea at Podvorye Restaurant, let her grievances about Chugunov "slip", and won his confirmation and an official investigation. At the Veche vote on Project Stuzha she read Chugunov's surprise vote against the project as Lelek's coercion. After Lelek's actions, the Rokot leadership's letter withdrew the codename and reminded members that motives and methods matter equally; Vodyanitsa recited its closing motto with Alyosha.

3.comment: Vodyanitsa: The last Water Imp of Snezhnograd
3.content:
Long ago Water Imps sang on Snezhnograd's stages, hummed in its alleys and splashed passers-by from the water. Then, after the Pale Star's lingering radiance went out, they left one by one, leaving behind sheet music to pay a meal debt, a flower for a grumpy Domovoy, and pearls for a jeweller. The city felt quietly incomplete until Vodyanitsa announced from the Korolevskiy Theater that the show would go on. Her kin say the city's hearts burn too hot and its voices clamour too loudly for Water Imps to thrive there.

Her rule for staying: find ten people; if one truly listens, stay. She sees fans who turned tickets into currency, but remembers when their love was sincere and stays for them too. Backstage she still talks to absent colleagues Paraskeva and Xenia, promising to hit their notes.

In Upstream Variations (7.1) she says she hears the departed Water Imps singing in the empty theater: they cry, laugh and argue, and she believes a song needs a listener to survive. She has memorised every piece a Water Imp ever performed there and stages special shows of their songs. She also fears that once she is no longer the adored Prima Donna, her own songs will be forgotten too.

4.content:
Vodyanitsa writes tickets by hand for people who love her singing but cannot get a seat. They are valid for almost every show: an empty seat if there is one, otherwise a place in the wings. She also keeps a handful of ordinary tickets in her pocket to hand to fans. She resents people who sell or flaunt them; to her a handwritten ticket simply means "I'd love you to come hear me sing."

Lishnaya was once a girl working part-time at the theater, who begged for a ticket daily and watched from behind the curtain when shows sold out. She grew into a guild head who used Vodyanitsa's tickets to win over merchants and climbed into the Zapolyarny elite, sending flowers instead of coming. Vodyanitsa never revoked her ticket, but Lishnaya never came backstage again.

In Upstream Variations she announces that certain handwritten tickets are void, and Odette threatens to print the names of anyone who makes trouble. She gives the Traveler a ticket that "will never expire".

5.content:
Mitya, a renowned energy scientist, attends every performance yet buries himself in notes. When she quizzed him over tea, he could name what Odette had performed but none of her songs. She sulked, then forgave him on learning his work concerned Project Stuzha, and he confirmed the Iskra plant's violations. She threatens to sing her loudest pieces to break his concentration.

In the afterlife theater she argued against his theory that he was already dead. Her Requiem later helped him find his way back through the storm. When Restaurant Zorya opened she made him say which song she had sung the day before he could eat.

6.comment: Vodyanitsa: Wraith's Nocturne and the Requiem
6.content:
After a rehearsal of "Spirit Seeker", a blizzard trapped the Korolevskiy audience. Unknown to them, they were in an afterlife version of the theater under Ronova's Curse of Death, and two people died each night. Vodyanitsa opened the theater's supplies and handed out free food. She defended Odette and kept people's spirits up. When Paimon's absence weighed on the Traveler, she said that when the Water Imps left she too had felt the world was empty. She sang a ceremonial Water Imp song that means roughly "may those we have lost watch over us and follow this song home". In the dream that followed she was a "guardian spirit" who revived the Traveler when a spirit called Night Prayer killed them, guided them through the dark, and then faded, "used up". She was found dead that morning.

Her Requiem guided Mitya back through the storm. Ronova later said the Water Imp's song had thrown things off a little and that she needed to review her attitude toward the Water Imp race. Everyone eventually woke in the real theater with fragmentary memories that returned once they were reminded.

7.content:
In the afterlife theater, the cheerful bodyguard Shram heard Vodyanitsa's nervous humming and read its emotion, which normally only Water Imps can do. He explained that he was dating a Water Imp, but talked of the human-fae civil war as current. Valeriy dated that war to over four hundred years ago, and Shram realised he was a ghost who had died protecting his lover from a mob hunting Water Imps in the theater. He named her as Litiya Ozerova. Vodyanitsa remembered "Auntie Ozerova", a kind elder with many children, so he walked into the storm at peace.

Afterwards Vodyanitsa admitted she was too little at the time to remember much of the conflict, and that history records little.

8.comment: Vodyanitsa: Vaselisa Vodyanovna and the Water Imps' covenant
8.content:
Water Imps once roamed freely from Dalegrad. Their lord Vodyanoy Dombertiev, "the Lackland", allied with King Miscislav the Blood-Devourer, and Water Imps fought for him. His daughter Vaselisa Vodyanovna, the "Zmey Maiden", mourned the dead on the frozen lake and led every Water Imp who would no longer bear arms to Emperor Monomakh, the Belyi Tsar. She refused crown, treasure and land and asked only that Water Imps never again serve another's desire by force, and that they sing for every soul with true love. The Tsar swore it. The Water Imps marched unarmed as couriers of dispatches and lovers' letters, river medics and singers who lulled soldiers to sleep. A history book adds that Miscislav slaughtered and plundered the Water Imps still loyal to him in revenge.

After the war Vodyanovna told them to sing as freely as the waters run, for every precious thing and every sincere heart. Vodyanitsa's parents repeated those words to her as a child.

9.content:
As Vodyanitsa describes them, Snezhnayan Water Imps are "ordinary people living ordinary lives", not fairytale sirens. They change tails into legs at no special price, though leaving the water is price enough. They express feelings chiefly through song, sense far through sound, understand Frostfin whale song, and are "experts at lulling people to sleep". Legend says their true tears become pearls, which Vodyanitsa laughed off.

She jokes that a broken promise to a Water Imp brings the old curse of Water Imps who abandoned their forms: no speech, no tears, and sea foam in the sun. She uses it as a mock threat when the Traveler promises to share new stories with her.

10.content: A secluded ice cave on Fellfrost Peak, beyond Snezhnograd's walls, where Vodyanitsa practises in a giant shell surrounded by Prime Ice echo pillars. She moved there after a girl began charging people to show them where she practised and resold her tickets. When some pillars cracked, the Traveler replaced them while her song marked the broken ones. Small animals flee her warm-ups when the pillars are out of tune and return when they ring true. Odette and Alyosha visit; she rescues puppies sheltering there from blizzards.

11.comment: Vodyanitsa: Rankova Zorya and Restaurant Zorya
11.content: After 7.0, Vodyanitsa dragged Odette and Alyosha into renovating the run-down station of Rankova Zorya and became its manager, doing most of the work herself. She arranged extra merchant trade routes, helped Mayskaya open a Bing-Bang Finchball booth, and opened Restaurant Zorya with a sign she painted of the three of them, armed with a copy of "100 Train Station Delicacies". The rumbling trains cover her rehearsals; she jokes her voice could make drivers forget to depart.

12.comment: Vodyanitsa: The Seals of Life case
12.content: In 7.1 Snezhnayans donated Seals of Life, their own life force, to the Tsaritsa's program. When word spread that someone was offering life-extension at a station to the frail and elderly, Vodyanitsa was horrified at betraying such trust. She disguised Alyosha as an old man, and once the seller, Avaz, was caught, she recognised his voice as a Northland Bank clerk who had once served her. He hinted a Harbinger was involved, and she concluded it was Regrator. After the seals returned to their owners, she heard the Traveler's account and lamented that Vesna's power had been taken; Vesna said it had never been hers.

13.comment: Vodyanitsa: Vesna and the ticket scalpers
13.content: Vesna's crackdown has pushed scalpers down to cryptic little ads. When scam victims arrived expecting a show, the event became a two-hour anti-scam lecture from Vesna, with Vodyanitsa chiming in and singing at the end. In an Anecdote she rewrites a scalper's contact details to her own flat and promises refunds, letters and front-row seats at full price, which she pays herself. Vesna says Vodyanitsa's songs move her to tears, and has noticed her slipping into the post-show crowd in a hat to sing harmony when the audience breaks into song.

14.content: Palomeya is a singer apprenticing under Vodyanitsa. In the Anecdote "I'll Take It All!" Vodyanitsa has her try on eleven outfits at Sadov-Arbat, insisting that humility taken to extremes is another form of arrogance and calling the fitting "rehearsing your stage presence". She pays for her performers' stage outfits and jewellery and does Palomeya's hair. Yevlena, a Vila, handles her orders and carries her purchases back to the theater.

15.content: Vodyanitsa answers fan letters despite the theater's advice and has practised calligraphy for it. She uses a rented address and fills five storerooms. Letters she remembers: a Fatui soldier she coached in singing who lost her voice in battle, whose compositions she recorded; a girl whose crayon drawings she still treasures, though the girl never wrote again after Vodyanitsa asked whether she wanted to paint her portrait out of fondness, love of art or ambition; and a poor student who sneaked into shows, to whom she sent free tickets. She talks to the letters sometimes and calls the rooms her private theater.

16.content: Harbingers get free admission but their families pay. Tartaglia always secures tickets for his family, and his sister Tonia is a devoted fan. Arlecchino brings children from her household (Lynette and Lyney once did a magic show on the stage) but watches "The Mountain Sparrow" alone. Sandrone arrives scowling and leaves a little calmer. Capitano sat straight as a pillar, and she sensed nothing could break him. She loved Columbina's moonlit singing. She once ended a Veche visit by greeting Sandrone and Tartaglia, then excused herself.

17.content: Vodyanitsa follows waterways to hear foreign singers. In Fontaine she gulped the water so loudly that a Special Security and Surveillance Patrol trainee dove in to save her, and she flicked away laughing. Hotel Debord once asked her to taste a cake, which she found dry and gritty. In Natlan she caught a little girl who fell into the water among the People of the Springs, was mobbed as "a real mermaid", and was shown around by Mualani, who promised to introduce her to Xilonen's music. In Liyue's Chenyu Vale she bathes in clean water and hunts for its fish adeptus. A Frostfin Whale named Hitova gave her rides.

18.comment: Vodyanitsa: Her diary and her parents
18.content: In the afterlife theater a girl and the Traveler found Vodyanitsa's diary, written as letters to her mother. It says Water Imp nobles were forced from their homeland by a change of power, that she will not forgive those who drove them away, and that she misses the manor's morning light. Backstage light reminds her of it. It calls her theater, fans and "the quiet dancing girl" hers, mentions the unnamed organisation she joined to look out for ordinary people, and admits she does not understand why the powerful do not bring greater happiness. She explained that her parents belonged to the aristocracy the Tsaritsa drove out and live where the post cannot reach.

19.content: A seven-day 7.1 World Quest. Vodyanitsa gives the Traveler a blank notebook and a handwritten ticket and tells the Lishnaya story in installments. She admits that the flowers from absent patrons make her feel she is singing to an empty theater. She meets Escoffier and Savanna and has them design a snow-swan cake for Odette. At night, alone, she wonders whether anyone would listen to "just the Water Imp who refused to leave". After talking with Odette, the Traveler has Aino build a miniature phonograph (Aino named it the Happy-Quacky Phonograph Ducky, though it looks like Vodyanitsa's necklace) so she can record her songs. In return she makes the Traveler serenade a Whopperflower and Paimon sing a silly song, records both, and hands back the phonograph stuffed with unreleased tracks.
